points.label: Charing
points.sub: the last, and seven times the cost of any other

footnote: Eleanor of Castile died in 1290. Her body was carried about 180 miles to Westminster, and Edward I built a stone cross at each place it rested overnight. F-131, F-132.
_correction: 2026-09-09: the first draft labelled the end dots 'Harby' and 'Westminster' and counted them among the twelve. Harby is where she died and Westminster is the destination; neither is a cross. The intermediate crosses are not named because this project has not sourced them — only Charing, as the last and most expensive, is in the fact sheet.
